newsitem.title: USA: Excessive rain slows Arkansas fieldwork.
newsitem.headline: Excessive rain slows Arkansas fieldwork.

text.p: Above normal temperatures and excessive rainfall slowed fieldwork in the week ended Sunday, Arkansas's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
Temperatures averaged one to six degrees above normal statewide. Soil moisture was rated nil very short, five percent short, 59 percent adequate and 36 percent surplus.
Soybeans were 51 percent harvested, compared with 50 percent for the five-year average. The crop rated two percent very poor, 12 poor, 25 fair, 45 good and 16 percent excellent.
Corn harvest was complete as of Sunday.
Cotton harvest was 80 percent complete, against 72 percent for the five-year average. The crop was rated four percent poor, 36 percent fair, 51 good and nine percent excellent.
Heavy rainfall caused some damage to the cotton crop in numerous counties, the report said. The Dumas Cotton Classing Office reported 353,432 bales classed as of October 24.
Winter wheat was 41 percent seeded as of Sunday, ahead of average of 47 percent. Twenty-one percent had emerged, against 28 percent average.
